newsitem.title: USA: Digital CEO sees strong 1997 earnings.
newsitem.headline: Digital CEO sees strong 1997 earnings.

text.p: Digital Equipment Corp Chief Executive Robert Palmer said he expects fiscal 1997 earnings per share to top analysts' consensus estimates of $1.00 per share, but the company's objective is to do better than $2.23 a share.

"We believe we can do better (than analysts' estimates)...and our objective is to do better than $2.23. But that's an objective not a forecast." The company earned $2.23 a share, excluding restructuring charges, for fiscal 1996.
Palmer spoke with reporters after the company's annual meeting here on Thursday.
Palmer said Digital's StrongARM computer chip, which runs on a low power base, will help the semiconductor division to return to profitability by the fourth quarter of fiscal year 1998.
Palmer said a realignment of Digital's sales force, which led to this year's unexpected disruption and contributed to the large fourth quarter and first quarter loss, is largerly completed.
He said orders are returning "to more normal patterns" but are not yet at 100 percent.
He said currency fluctuations, which cost the company $70 million in the first quarter, will not be material on a sequential basis in the second quarter.
In response to a shareholder question, Palmer, who also holds the titles of chairman and president, said the board of directors is not discussing naming a president.
Some reports have criticised Palmer for taking on too many responsibilities.
